question: A solar power station with a capacity of 400 MW is being promoted in Antichasia, in the regional unit of Trikala. The total designated area covers around 1 550 hectares, of which 600 hectares will be taken up by the power station buildings and equipment.

From the information I have been provided with, it looks as though the entire area is located within a Natura 2000 Special Protection Area (SPA) and approximately 220 hectares also fall within a Special Area of Conservation (SAC). The site is located just 215 metres from the edge of a settlement and another power station is being developed less than 8 km away.

The environmental impact study was submitted hastily and just eight months after the producer authorisation was issued. Potential consequences of the project include the destruction of habitats, flooding, species displacement, water pollution, reduction of land for crop cultivation and livestock farming and permanent visual degradation. In view of this, can the Commission answer the following: 1.

How does it check full compliance with all applicable EU procedures (Directives 2011/92/EU, 92/43/EEC and 2009/147/EC), including the appropriate assessment of Article 6 of the Habitats Directive for projects within Natura areas?
Does it intend to take the necessary steps to protect the environment and ecosystem, which is clearly at risk?
Will it consider the possibility of a breach of procedure and ask for the immediate suspension of permitting procedures until full compliance is ensured?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (8.10.2026) Industrial installations for the production of electricity, steam and hot water (projects not included in Annex I) are listed in Annex II.3.a of the Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) Directive1.

According to Article 4 of the EIA Directive, prior to granting a consent for such projects, Member States must determine whether an EIA2 is necessary, based on a caseby-case analysis or by setting specific criteria3.

In case Natura 2000 sites are likely to be significantly affected, such projects shall be subject to an appropriate assessment of their implications for the sites and be authorised in accordance with the Habitats Directive4.

The revised Renewable Energy Directive5,6, further simplifies and shortens administrative permitgranting procedures for renewable energy projects, without prejudice to the rights for public participation under the Aarhus Convention7.

Member States are primarily responsible to ensure compliance with EU law, including verifying individual cases of potential breach of the relevant rules or taking the necessary steps for enforcement, and the appropriate measures to address any matter that has arisen.
In its role as guardian of the Treaties, the Commission may decide to take appropriate action if any systemic problems are identified, in line with its enforcement priorities8.
1 Directive 2011/92/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 December 2011 on the assessment

of the effects of certain public and private projects on the environment, OJ L 26, 28.1.2012, p. 1–21, as amended by Directive 2014/52/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16 April 2014, OJ L 124, 25.4.2014, p. 1–18. 2 Including public consultation. 3 Such as the location, size or type of project.
4 Articles 6(3) and (4) , Council Directive 92/43/EEC of 21 May 1992 on the conservation of natural habitats and of wild fauna and flora. OJ L 206, 22.7.1992, p. 7–50.

5 Directive (EU) 2023/2413 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 18 October 2023 amending Directive (EU) 2018/2001, Regulation (EU) 2018/1999 and Directive 98/70/EC as regards the promotion of energy from renewable sources, and repealing Council Directive (EU) 2015/652, OJ L, 2023/2413, 31.10.2023.

6 Council Regulation (EU) 2022/2577 of 22 December 2022 laying down a framework to accelerate the deployment of renewable energy, OJ L 335, 29.12.2022, p. 36–44. The application of certain provisions of this Regulation has been extended until 30 June 2025. 7 https://unece.org/environment-policy/public-participation/aarhus-convention/text.

8 Communication from the Commission - EU law: Better results through better application, OJ C 18, 19.1.2017, p. 10–20, and Communication from the Commission - Enforcing EU law for a Europe that delivers, 13.10.2022, COM(2022) 518 final.
